questions.q: What makes a subscription "standard" rather than data-driven?
options: It has exactly one set of report parameters, delivery options, and recipients that never varies from run to run
It can only be created by a report server administrator
It can only deliver to a Windows file share, never e-mail
It automatically adjusts its recipient list based on a database query
questions.explain: A standard subscription uses static values — one fixed set of report presentation options, delivery options, and parameters every time it runs, unlike a data-driven subscription.

questions.q: Which two requirements must a report meet before New Subscription is even available?
options: The data source must use stored or no credentials, and any parameters must have default values
The report must already have at least one existing subscription
The report must be published to a My Reports folder
The report must use a data-driven dataset
questions.explain: Because a subscription runs unattended, the data source can't require someone to type in credentials, and any parameters need defaults since nobody is there to fill them in.

questions.q: When you create a new subscription, what happens to the Owner field?
options: It defaults to the current user and can't be edited at creation time
It must be typed in manually before the subscription can be saved
It is always set to the report server administrator
It is left blank until the first successful run
questions.explain: The Owner field defaults to whoever creates the subscription and is locked at creation — you can change it afterward through the subscription's properties, but not while creating it.

questions.q: On the Subscriptions management page, what does the Result column show?
options: The outcome or error message from the subscription's most recent run
The number of recipients the subscription delivered to
The report's rendering format
Whether the subscription is shared or report-specific
questions.explain: The Result column is the first place to check when a subscription didn't behave as expected — it holds the status or error from the last time it ran.

questions.q: What does Run Now do on the Subscriptions page?
options: Fires the subscription immediately instead of waiting for its schedule
Deletes the subscription after one final run
Converts a standard subscription into a data-driven one
Pauses the subscription's shared schedule
questions.explain: Run Now triggers the subscription on demand — useful during setup and testing so you don't have to wait for the scheduled time to come around.
